text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, learning patterns and relationships between words from their training data. When you give an LLM a prompt, it uses those patterns to generate a response. In prompt engineering, you carefully craft that input to get better answers, such as adding specific instructions or examples. LLMs can write, summarize, and translate impressively well. However, they have limits: they may produce false facts, lack real understanding, and cannot verify information on their own, so their output always needs checking.
